metric.why: PPAs are how the boom finances new generation and how operators back renewable claims. Nuclear agreements, including restarts and small modular commitments, became the signature deals of the AI era.
metric.definition: Long-term contracts by which operators secure generation, nuclear, solar, wind, or gas, for current and future facilities.

reading.body:
Power purchase agreements are the financial mechanism through which AI operators lock in generation for data centers, making them the leading indicator of where new compute capacity will actually operate.

PPAs represent a hard constraint on AI scaling. An operator cannot build a facility without securing power, and securing power requires committing capital years in advance through these contracts. The mix of generation types in new PPAs—nuclear, solar, wind, or gas—reveals which technologies the industry believes can deliver the reliability and scale required. Nuclear agreements, including restarts and small modular reactor commitments, emerged as the signature deals of the AI era, signaling operator conviction about future load and generation costs.

What this metric does not capture is whether signed PPAs actually deliver power on schedule. Interconnection delays, permitting failures, and construction overruns can leave an operator with a contract but no grid connection. It also does not show the price operators paid relative to spot markets, the duration of commitments, or the geographic distribution of demand versus supply. The data reflects intent and financial commitment, not the state of the grid itself.
